title: Use an opportunity before it changes or act within an interval

variants.label: うちに · before the opportunity changes

segments.role: うちに makes Dad’s absence an opportunity that will end. The aim is to act before that state changes. It does not itself state an exact duration or require panic; the surprise-party context supplies the reason to finish now.

example.translation: Let us make the birthday decorations while Dad is still out.
example.note: You are preparing a surprise and want to finish before he comes back.

variants.change: うちに makes Dad’s absence an opportunity that will end. The aim is to act before that state changes. It does not itself state an exact duration or require panic; the surprise-party context supplies the reason to finish now.

variants.label: 間に · within that interval

segments.role: 間に places the action within the outing interval. It can also describe using an opportunity, so both versions are natural here; うちに more strongly foregrounds doing it before the situation changes. They are not interchangeable everywhere: 忘れないうちに naturally means before forgetting. The gradual-change use of うちに is outside this comparison.

example.translation: Let us make the birthday decorations during the time Dad is out.
example.note: His outing gives you a time window in which to make the decorations.

question: Which interpretation best captures the extra focus of うちに in the surprise-party scene?
answers: Make use of Dad’s absence before he returns and the opportunity changes.
Keep making decorations continuously for every moment of his absence.
Wait until Dad has returned, then start the decorations.
feedback: うちに foregrounds acting while the useful state still holds. 間に locates an event within a time interval; it does not require that the action fill the entire interval. Both work naturally for these decorations.
